questions.stem: What is Unified Data Architecture about?
options: Choosing a single database vendor for the whole organisation
Covering all aspects of data with respect to organisational architectures
Replacing all data warehouses with a data lake
Migrating every workload to the public cloud
questions.explanation: Unified Data Architecture covers all aspects of data with respect to organisational architectures, and there is no single pre-defined version for everyone.

questions.stem: Is there a pre-defined Unified Data Architecture that suits every organisation?
options: No, there is no pre-defined Unified Data Architecture for everyone
questions.explanation: The topic states that there is no pre-defined Unified Data Architecture for everyone.

questions.stem: Which architecture is described for source applications?
questions.explanation: The architecture for source applications is OLTP, while data warehouses use OLAP and cubes.

questions.stem: At what level should a Unified Data Architecture be designed before the individual data architectures?
questions.explanation: One must design Unified Data Architecture for a 30,000-feet view before designing data architectures for each component.

questions.stem: How does Unified Data Architecture relate to the individual data architectures, by analogy with Enterprise Architecture?
options: Each data architecture may ignore it
All data architectures in an organisation must follow Unified Data Architecture standards
It is a replacement for Enterprise Architecture
It applies only to the data lake
It applies only to cloud workloads
questions.explanation: Just as Business, Application, Technical and Data Architectures follow Enterprise Architecture standards, all data architectures must follow Unified Data Architecture standards.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an approach to building a Unified Data Architecture?
options: Logical Data Warehousing and Data Virtualisation Architecture
questions.explanation: Listed approaches include legacy enhancement, logical data warehousing and virtualisation, organisational-driven, business or LOB-driven, multi-cloud and hybrid; a single-vendor mandate is not among them.

questions.stem: Which is given as an example of Business or LOB-driven Data Architecture?
questions.explanation: Business or line-of-business-driven data architecture examples are Data Mesh and Data Mart, whereas Data Lake and Data Warehouse are organisational-driven.

questions.stem: In most Unified Data Architectures, what does the Data Consumption Layer consist of?
questions.explanation: The elements are Data Producers (source systems), Data Consumption Layer (ETL/ELT processes), Data Storages, Advanced Analysis, Data Serving Layer and Data Management.

questions.stem: Which of these belongs to the Data Management element of a Unified Data Architecture?
options: Metadata, data quality, security and privacy, governance, master and reference data
questions.explanation: Data Management covers metadata, data quality, data security and privacy, data governance, master data and reference data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed among the data architectures an organisation may have for Data Lake-style platforms?
options: Delta Lake, Data Mesh, Data Vault, Business Vault, Data Hub and Data Fabric
questions.explanation: The Data Lake family of architectures includes Delta Lake, Data Mesh, Data Vault, Business Vault, Data Hub and Data Fabric.
